Engineering Handoff

DisMyth — Backend Build Brief

This document specifies the backend a developer needs to turn the existing DisMyth prototype into a live product on dismyth.app. The frontend (landing, app, methodology) is built and deployable today; everything below is the server-side work that makes verdicts, accounts, and publishing real.

1 · What already exists

Frontend, done: full mobile app UI (onboarding, feed, spread map, alerts, plans), the verdict experience (multi-AI consensus, confidence range, evidence, origin & mutation timeline, media forensics, neutrality meter), share-check interception, dispute/human-review flow, accuracy ledger, and a public landing + methodology site. All screens are static, editable HTML and host as-is on any static CDN.

Not real yet: live claim verification (the demo call only runs inside the design tool), the regional feed/map/ledger data, authentication, billing, and social auto-posting. These are the four backend layers scoped here.

2 · System architecture

Frontend — static site (current HTML) on Vercel / Netlify / Cloudflare Pages, served at dismyth.app. Talks to the API over HTTPS/JSON.

API service — stateless HTTP API (Node/TypeScript or Python/FastAPI). Handles claims, accounts, billing, publishing. Deploy on Fly.io / Render / AWS.

Verification workers — a job queue (e.g. BullMQ/Redis or SQS) running the multi-model check, retrieval, and forensics asynchronously so the API stays responsive.

Data — PostgreSQL (claims, verdicts, users, corrections), Redis (cache + queue), object storage (uploaded images/video), and a vector store (pgvector) for claim de-duplication and matching.

3 · Core API endpoints

POST /v1/checks — submit a claim (text / url / image / video). Returns {checkId, status:"queued"}.
GET /v1/checks/:id — poll verdict; returns the full verdict object (see §5) once status:"complete".
GET /v1/feed?region=... — regional feed of recent public verdicts.
GET /v1/trends?region=... — spread-map hotspots + trend-radar velocities.
POST /v1/disputes — escalate a verdict to human review.
POST /v1/broadcasts — (Pro) publish a correction to connected social channels.
GET /v1/ledger — public accuracy metrics + corrections log.
POST /v1/auth/*, /v1/billing/* — accounts, sessions, subscriptions, webhooks.

4 · The verification pipeline (the core IP)

This is the heart of DisMyth and where most engineering effort goes. On each /v1/checks job:

  1. Normalise input. Text → clean claim string. URL → fetch + extract the article/post text and metadata. Image/video → store to object storage, generate a hash.
  2. De-duplicate. Embed the claim and match against previously-checked claims (pgvector). A near-match returns the cached verdict instantly — this is what makes DisMyth fast and cheap at scale.
  3. Retrieve evidence. Query trusted-source APIs and web search (official/gov, scientific, fact-check databases, reputable news). Rank each source by a credibility weight (Official/Scientific 90–95, Forensic 86, News 78…) — the weights already shown in the UI.
  4. Multi-model consensus. Send claim + retrieved evidence to 3–4 LLMs (Claude, GPT, Grok, Gemini) with a strict JSON schema. Each returns verdict + confidence. Compute agreement %; if models disagree past a threshold, mark Contested and auto-route to human review (never auto-broadcast).
  5. Media forensics (image/video only). Run reverse-image search, AI-generation detection, manipulation/ELA analysis, and frame matching for out-of-context reuse. Produce the three forensic signal scores.
  6. Origin & mutation trace. Use platform search APIs to find earliest appearances and reworded variants; assemble the ORIGIN → MUTATION → SPREAD timeline.
  7. Assemble & persist the verdict object, cache it, and (if public) add to the regional feed.

Prompt contract: the prototype already defines the exact JSON schema the models must return (verdict, confidence, checks, origin, evidence[], bias). Reuse it verbatim — it drives the UI directly.

5 · Verdict data model

{
  id, claim, verdict: True|False|Misleading|Unverified|Contested,
  confidence: 0-100, confidenceBand: {lo, hi},
  consensus: {agreement, models:[{name, verdict, confidence}]},
  checks: [string], whatWouldChange: string,
  evidence: [{source, type, weight, url}],
  forensics: {headline, signals:[{label, pct}], note} | null,
  timeline: [{tag, time, text}], bias: {leaning, note},
  region, createdAt, status
}

Every field maps 1:1 to a component already rendered in the app — build the API to this shape and the frontend needs almost no change.

6 · Third-party services

LLMs: Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI, xAI (Grok), Google (Gemini) APIs. Retrieval: a web-search API (Brave/Bing/SerpAPI) + fact-check feeds (Google Fact Check Tools API, ClaimReview schema). Forensics: reverse-image (TinEye/Google Vision), an AI-image detector, plus ELA/metadata libs. Social publishing: X API, Meta Graph API (FB/IG/Threads) — start app-review now; approval is slow. Payments: Razorpay (India-first) or Stripe. Infra: Postgres, Redis, S3-compatible storage.

7 · Accounts, plans & billing

Email/OAuth auth (Google, Apple). Three tiers already designed: Free (unlimited checks, feed, map), DisMyth+ ₹149/mo (geo-alerts, priority, ad-free), Pro ₹4,999/mo (auto-post, monitoring dashboard, API, team seats). Gate features by plan; meter API usage for Pro. Wire billing webhooks to update entitlements.

8 · Human review & the public ledger

Contested and disputed claims enter a review queue for senior fact-checkers + vetted community reviewers; a verdict is held from broadcast until resolved. Every published verdict, correction, and its reason is written to the append-only ledger that powers the public accuracy page — this is core to the IFCN signatory goal, so build it as an auditable, immutable log from day one.

9 · Phased delivery plan

Phase 1 · week 1

Ship the site. Deploy current frontend to dismyth.app + a waitlist form. No backend needed. (See the deploy guide.)

Phase 2 · weeks 2–5

Real single-claim check. /v1/checks for text + URL, retrieval, multi-model consensus, verdict persistence. This alone is a shippable product.

Phase 3 · weeks 6–9

Accounts + billing, de-dup cache, public feed & ledger, dispute queue.

Phase 4 · weeks 10+

Media forensics, origin tracing, spread map, and social auto-posting (pending platform approvals) + the browser extension for share-check.

10 · Non-functional notes

Cost control: the de-dup cache is essential — most viral claims are checked once and served from cache thousands of times. Rate limits & abuse: per-IP and per-account throttling on /checks. Neutrality: log every model's raw output for auditability; never let a single model's answer publish unreviewed. Privacy: uploaded media is scanned then purged on a retention schedule. Compliance: methodology, corrections policy, and funding must stay public per IFCN principles (already reflected in the methodology page).

Deliver §4 (pipeline) and §5 (data model) to spec and the existing frontend becomes a live product with minimal rework. Questions on any section → build against the prototype; it is the source of truth for behaviour and shapes.
